title: Making Codebases Agent Ready – Eno Reyes, Factory AI
talk_summary: Eno Reyes argues agent performance is limited less by model choice than by codebase validation: opinionated linters, tests, docs, AGENTS.md, and spec-driven constraints let agents self-check and parallelize. He recommends systematically closing validation gaps with agents and treating the environment feedback loop as the main lever for reliable autonomous software work.

takeaways.what_they_do: Build opinionated automated validators—linters, tests, OpenAPI/schema checks, AGENTS.md—so agents can verify their own work before review.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Do you have llinters that are so opinionated that a coding agent will always make code that is exactly at the level of what your senior engineers will produce?
specifying the constraints by which you would like to be validated and what should be built

takeaways.what_they_do: Ask coding agents to find missing linters/tests/opinionated checks and generate initial tests; a weak test is better than none because it creates a feedback signal.
takeaways.evidence_quote: could you figure out where we're not being opinionated enough about our llinters. You can ask a coding agent to generate tests.

takeaways.what_they_do: Dedicate agent capacity to improving the repo environment—docs, tests, lint rules—so every future agent run benefits.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If you have better agents, they will make the environment better which will make the agents better

takeaways.what_they_do: Give AI reviewers explicit documentation and pointers; agents will not reliably invent validation criteria or project conventions from thin air.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you want a really highquality AI generated code review, you need documentation for your AI systems

takeaways.what_they_do: Do not scale multi-agent decomposition or parallel PRs until simple single-task execution plus validation succeeds nearly 100% of the time.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if that does not work nearly 100% of the time you can sort of forget successfully using these other things at scale
